papers.title: Coupling of Cell Energetics with Membrane Metabolic Sensing
papers.authors: Maria Roselle Abraham; Vitaly A. Selivanov; Denice M. Hodgson; Darko Pucar; Leonid V. Zingman; Bé Wieringa; Petras P. Dzeja; Alexey E. Alekseev; André Terzic
papers.abstract: Transduction of metabolic signals is essential in preserving cellular homeostasis. Yet, principles governing integration and synchronization of membrane metabolic sensors with cell metabolism remain elusive. Here, analysis of cellular nucleotide fluxes and nucleotide-dependent gating of the ATP-sensitive K+ (K(ATP)) channel, a prototypic metabolic sensor, revealed a diffusional barrier within the submembrane space, preventing direct reception of cytosolic signals. Creatine kinase phosphotransfer, captured by 18O-assisted 31P NMR, coordinated tightly with ATP turnover, reflecting the cellular energetic status. The dynamics of high energy phosphoryl transfer through the creatine kinase relay permitted a high fidelity transmission of energetic signals into the submembrane compartment synchronizing K(ATP) channel activity with cell metabolism. Knock-out of the creatine kinase M-CK gene disrupted signal delivery to K(ATP) channels and generated a cellular phenotype with increased electrical vulnerability. Thus, in the compartmentalized cell environment, phosphotransfer systems shunt diffusional barriers and secure regimented signal transduction integrating metabolic sensors with the cellular energetic network.
papers.categories: Cell biology; Adenylate kinase; Cytosol; Biology; Biochemistry

papers.title: STUDIES OF THE METABOLISM OF HUMAN ERYTHROCYTE MEMBRANES*
papers.authors: Stanley L. Schrier
papers.abstract: These investigations were undertaken to dis-cover whether the membrane of the mature human erythrocyte is capable of metabolic activity that could possibly provide the means for active trans-port. Hoffman (2) has clearly shown that ATP pro-vides energy for sodium transport, and it has been assumed that ATP for this process is sup-plied from within the erythrocyte. It seemed reasonable to examine membranes not only for possible sources of ATP production, but also for segments of metabolic pathways that could func-tion as specific transport systems. Two methods have been in general use for the study of the enzymic composition of membranes (3). In one, whole cells are incubated with sub-strates or inhibitors to which the membrane is known to be impermeable. Any change in the ex-ternal medium is then taken to represent enzymic activity present on the outer surface of the mem-brane. In the second method., labeled, permeable substrates are added to the medium, and after relatively short intervals, labeled compounds are extracted from the interior of cells and identified. The enzymic activity of the membrane is then de-duced from the observed changes in substrates. Both methods have been useful, but neither can provide information about the organization of en-zymes in the membranes. For this purpose, it is necessary to prepare and study erythrocyte mem-branes themselves. In the present study, morphologically intact homogeneous membranes, virtually free of he-moglobin, were prepared by dialysis of human erythrocytes against increasingly hypotonic saline

papers.title: Heme in pathophysiology: a matter of scavenging, metabolism and trafficking across cell membranes
papers.authors: Deborah Chiabrando; Francesca Vinchi; Veronica Fiorito; Sonia Mercurio; Emanuela Tolosano
papers.abstract: Heme (iron-protoporphyrin IX) is an essential co-factor involved in multiple biological processes: oxygen transport and storage, electron transfer, drug and steroid metabolism, signal transduction, and micro RNA processing. However, excess free-heme is highly toxic due to its ability to promote oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation, thus leading to membrane injury and, ultimately, apoptosis. Thus, heme metabolism needs to be finely regulated. Intracellular heme amount is controlled at multiple levels: synthesis, utilization by hemoproteins, degradation and both intracellular and intercellular trafficking. This review focuses on recent findings highlighting the importance of controlling intracellular heme levels to counteract heme-induced oxidative stress. The contributions of heme scavenging from the extracellular environment, heme synthesis and incorporation into hemoproteins, heme catabolism and heme transport in maintaining adequate intracellular heme content are discussed. Particular attention is put on the recently described mechanisms of heme trafficking through the plasma membrane mediated by specific heme importers and exporters. Finally, the involvement of genes orchestrating heme metabolism in several pathological conditions is illustrated and new therapeutic approaches aimed at controlling heme metabolism are discussed.

papers.title: New insights into coupling and uncoupling of cerebral blood flow and metabolism in the brain
papers.authors: Poornima Venkat; Michael Chopp; Jieli Chen
papers.abstract: The brain has high metabolic and energy needs and requires continuous cerebral blood flow (CBF), which is facilitated by a tight coupling between neuronal activity, CBF, and metabolism. Upon neuronal activation, there is an increase in energy demand, which is then met by a hemodynamic response that increases CBF. Such regional CBF increase in response to neuronal activation is observed using neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission tomography. The mechanisms and mediators (eg, nitric oxide, astrocytes, and ion channels) that regulate CBF-metabolism coupling have been extensively studied. The neurovascular unit is a conceptual model encompassing the anatomical and metabolic interactions between the neurons, vascular components, and glial cells in the brain. It is compromised under disease states such as stroke, diabetes, hypertension, dementias, and with aging, all of which trigger a cascade of inflammatory responses that exacerbate brain damage. Hence, tight regulation and maintenance of neurovascular coupling is central for brain homeostasis. This review article also discusses the waste clearance pathways in the brain such as the glymphatic system. The glymphatic system is a functional waste clearance pathway that removes metabolic wastes and neurotoxins from the brain along paravascular channels. Disruption of the glymphatic system burdens the brain with accumulating waste and has been reported in aging as well as several neurological diseases.
papers.categories: Glymphatic system; Cerebral blood flow; Neuroscience; Homeostasis; Premovement neuronal activity

papers.title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
papers.authors: Kevin Goldstein; Vishnu Jejjala; Suresh Nampuri
papers.abstract: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

papers.title: BRUCE (Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator): spatiotemporal interpolation of air temperature from heterogeneous sensor networks for operational heat monitoring
papers.authors: Ayrton Sena Gouveia; Rafael Santos de Oliveira; Lucas Menezes-Silva; Maira Alejandra Moreno Castillo; Felipe de Carvalho Vommaro Marincola; João Henrique de Araújo Morais; Valéria Saraceni; Gislani Mateus Oliveira Aguilar; Caroline Dias Ferreira; Oswaldo Gonçalves Cruz
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of intra-urban temperature variability is essential for heat-health surveillance, yet official monitoring networks are too sparse to resolve fine-scale gradients, particularly in Global South cities. We present BRUCE, a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, fitted with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) and a Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) spatial component, that fuses four heterogeneous temperature sources for Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: official weather stations, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen-science personal weather stations and ERA5-Land reanalysis. The model accounts for class- and station-specific measurement bias and estimates a continuous spatial field that evolves day to day through an autoregressive (AR1) structure. Fitted independently to nine monthly windows (January, June, November; 2023--2025), the elevation coefficient was significant in all windows and of consistent magnitude in eight ($-$1.08 to $-$1.38 \textdegree{}C per SD). In leave-region-out cross-validation against LCZ4r, accuracy was comparable (RMSE differences within station-level bootstrap uncertainty in all three windows), while BRUCE produced predictions at every held-out station, including those where LCZ4r is masked, and preserved finer-scale spatial structure than LCZ4r's discrete zone classification. Applied to 241 primary care territories, BRUCE's posterior exceedance probabilities allowed 96 to be classified with high confidence (model-based classifications), whereas a constant-width interval derived from LCZ4r cross-validation errors supported confident classification of none. The framework offers a statistically principled, operationally viable basis for intra-urban heat monitoring in data-heterogeneous settings.

papers.title: Bridging the Discovery Gap in Solid Dataspaces with a Semantic Data Catalog
papers.authors: Florian Hölken; Alexander Paulus; Tobias Meisen; André Pomp
papers.abstract: Dataspaces are an emerging concept to enable secure and controlled data sharing between multiple stakeholders. However, most existing dataspace architectures, such as those based on the concepts of IDSA (International Data Spaces Association) and Gaia-X, are heavily concept-driven and require significant effort to implement, making it difficult to quickly build a functional dataspace. Solid (Social Linked Data) offers a compelling alternative by providing a lighter and more practical approach. However, for Solid to function as a true dataspace, like traditional dataspaces, it must be built in a decentralized manner, i.e., the dataspace must consist of more than a single Solid server. However, this decentralization introduces a key challenge: Data Discovery. Unlike traditional dataspace architectures, which often include predefined components such as data catalogs to facilitate data discovery and access, Solid does not inherently provide such mechanisms. As a result, managing and locating relevant data across multiple Solid servers and pods becomes a significant barrier to usability. To address this gap, we present a FAIR-compliant data catalog for Solid. Our catalog follows the FAIR principles (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability) by integrating semantic models that describe all available data sources within the Solid ecosystem. This approach enables enhanced data discovery, improves accessibility through standardized metadata, enhances interoperability between different data sources, and promotes data reuse across applications. By bridging this critical gap, our catalog improves the usability of Solid-based dataspaces, making them a viable option for decentralized and open data ecosystems, such as smart city applications.

papers.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
papers.authors: Luisa Eck; Paul Fendley
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.authors: Emiel Claasen; Mehregan Doroudiani; Claude Duhr; Axel Kleinschmidt; Franca Lippert; Oliver Schlotterer; Yoann Sohnle
papers.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Kai Lu; Chenyang Ma; Ioannis Havoutis
papers.abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

papers.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Jiahao Huang; Jun Wang
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.authors: John M. Martyn; Rod Rofougaran; Samuel Stein; Di Luo
papers.abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis to Decipher the Anti-Biofilm Mechanism of Anthraquinone-2- Carboxylic Acid against Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.authors: Shen XC; Song ZM; Ding JJ; Gao XM; Li XL; Xiong WJ; Fan XH; Li HF; Zhang YZ; Shen L; Jiang B; Wang KL
papers.abstract: The biofilms of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) exhibit high drug resistance and cause nosocomial infections in humans, posing a persistent threat to human health globally. It is essential to develop anti-biofilm lead compound with high efficacy and well- characterized mechanisms to disrupt existing biofilms and eradicate persistent infections. In this study, the action mechanism of a promising anti-biofilm agent anthraquinone-2-carboxylic acid (ACA) against MRSA was systematically investigated through integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses, coupling with the validation of real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and the experiment of the accumulation of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, selected biofilm-associated biomarkers were rigorously validated using targeted parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) with mass spectrometry. The results of proteomics demonstrated that ACA primarily affected the KEGG pathways related to membrane transport, nucleotide metabolism, amino acid metabolism, lipid metabolism, and energy metabolism. Notably, metabolic profiling showed changes consistent to proteomic findings, particularly in the pathways linked to oxidative phosphorylation and pyrimidine metabolism. Overall, the integrative analysis of multi-omics datasets, combined with experimental validation, suggested that ACA-mediated MRSA biofilm eradication involve three complementary processes, including disruption of bacterial membrane integrity, inhibition of de novo nucleotide biosynthesis, and ROS accumulation coupled with interference in energy metabolism. These processes collectively resulted in MRSA biofilm dispersal. This study firstly elucidates the molecular mechanism underlying the disruption of MRSA biofilms of anthraquinone compounds, establishing a robust theoretical framework for the rational design of ACA-based anti-biofilm agents against MRSA.

papers.title: Freeze-thaw aging enhances microplastic phytotoxicity in rice via root metabolism and DNA methylation.
papers.authors: Wang Z; Gao Z; Wang Z; Wang M; Yao Z; Huang Z; Yu T; Li J; Liu H; Li Z; Chen J
papers.abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling (FTC) accelerates microplastic (MP) aging in cold-region soils, yet the mechanisms underlying their amplified phytotoxicity remain elusive. This study integrated physicochemical characterization, metabolomics, and DNA methylation sequencing to evaluate the root toxicity of pristine and FTC-aged polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene in rice (Oryza sativa). FTC aging induced surface oxidation and structural fragmentation, increasing hydrodynamic diameters by 8.8-26.7% and elevating negative surface charge by 5.17-5.36 mV. The aged PVC elicited the most severe phytotoxicity, disrupting root membrane integrity and suppressing superoxide dismutase activity by up to 54%. Metabolomic profiling revealed pronounced malate depletion coupled with lactate accumulation, indicating alterations in central carbon metabolism consistent with a potential shift toward glycolysis-associated metabolism, alongside significant perturbations in branched-chain amino acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing demonstrated that DNA methylation reprogramming was dominated by the CHH context, accounting for > 96% of all differentially methylated regions. Correlation network analysis revealed that aged PVC induced targeted CHH promoter hypermethylation in key redox hubs (e.g., NTRC, Trx M3), effectively decoupling antioxidant defense signaling from core energy metabolism. The work pinpoints that FTC-aged MP induced CHH methylation could connect to root metabolic reprogramming, establishing a basis for assessing risks of MPs in cold-climate agriculture.

papers.title: Biomimetic Subcellular Chemomechanical Nano-Regulator for Allergic Rhinitis Treatment.
papers.authors: Ge S; Du H; Liu J; Zhu F; Yang Z; Gao X; Guo X; Shi L; Qi W; Zhao Y; Liu C; Xia M
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a highly prevalent and debilitating chronic inflammatory disease; however, its complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely explored, resulting in a significant lack of effective therapeutic strategies in clinical practice. Here, we found that the submucosal extracellular matrix undergoes profound pathological stiffening during AR development and is associated with severe epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and physical barrier collapse. Based on this pathomechanical observation, we developed a spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator (SCM) to reconstruct the damaged mucosal barrier. Capitalizing on its precise targeting and cascade-responsive capabilities, SCM provides immediate anti-inflammatory activity to stabilize stressed epithelial cells. Beyond this acute intervention, the regulator scavenges intracellular free radicals, attenuates pathological mitochondria-associated membrane (MAM) over-coupling, and restores mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis. In parallel, the Mn-containing nanocore and pirfenidone jointly attenuate fibroblast activation and abnormal extracellular-matrix stiffening. Formulation-resolved cellular and animal studies distinguished a predominant TA-associated contribution to early inflammatory and epithelial-barrier responses from a predominant PFD-associated contribution to later matrix remodeling. Full SCM combined these stage-associated response domains while rebuilding epithelial-barrier integrity and shifting systemic immune readouts toward tolerance. These findings provide a preclinical mechanobiology-guided framework for treating AR and other mechanically driven inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: RAB11-RAB30 partnership drives stress-induced endosomal remodeling via a phosphoinositide switch.
papers.authors: Alemany C; Poulard C; Kalubi Kabambi A; Guerrera IC; Romao M; Raposo G; Da Graça J; Claude-Taupin A; Stevenin V; Delevoye C; Morel E
papers.abstract: Upon acute stress, cells rapidly engage autophagy to preserve integrity and adapt. This is tightly coupled to membrane remodeling, notably mobilization and reorganization of endosomal compartments supporting autophagosome formation. Here, we uncover a stress-specific partnership between the small GTPases RAB11 and RAB30 that orchestrates endosomal trafficking during response to physiological stress. TurboID-based proximity labeling of RAB11A combined with mass spectrometry identifies RAB30, a Golgi-localized protein, as a critical stress-specific partner. Upon stress, RAB30 relocalizes to RAB11-positive endosomes and is required for autophagic response and cell survival. Using stress conditions-starvation, shear stress, and osmotic stress-we show that RAB11 and RAB30 are indispensable for cell survival and autophagy, extending RAB11's role beyond recycling to the cell surface. Under shear and nutritional stress, RAB11 compartments undergo morphodynamic remodeling governed by local PI3P/PI4P turnover essential for RAB30 mobilization. Our findings highlight a phosphoinositide-driven RAB11-RAB30 axis integrating membrane trafficking and autophagy under stress, revealing a dedicated endosomal circuit for adaptive membrane supply.

papers.title: Gadolinium-Based Contrast Agents Stimulate Adaptive Immune Response through Release of DAMP Signals in Neuronal SH-SY5Y Cells.
papers.authors: Arojojoye AS; Arino T; Selvam A; Trinh A; Abergel RJ
papers.abstract: The use of gadolinium-based compounds as contrast agents in magnetic resonance imaging scans has been popularized owing to the superior anatomical images they produce and tracking of a broad spectrum of clinical conditions. While these compounds are considered safe when administered at appropriate dose levels, toxicity has been reported for patients with impaired renal functions. Toxicogenomic and intracellular accumulation studies have also implicated genes relevant to lipid synthesis, disruption of cytoplasmic membrane integrity, and accumulation in the neuronal interstitium, kidney, liver, and skin. These findings have prompted widespread studies into the mechanism of intracellular accumulation and cytotoxicity of gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs). In the present work, neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells were treated with macrocyclic Gd chelate gadoterate meglumine, linear Gd chelate gadopentetic acid, and GdCl3 salt to decipher their ability to activate the release of danger-associated molecular pattern signals (DAMPs), key steps in the induction of immunologic cell death (ICD). Furthermore, intracellular accumulation and localization of the GBCAs in SH-SY5Y cells were studied using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Our results showed no significant cytotoxicity to SH-SY5Y cells until 5 mM for all compounds tested except gadopentetic acid. Cells undergoing early apoptosis were observed with both gadoterate meglumine and gadopentetic acid at 1 and 10 mM compared to nontreated control samples. Evidence for mild induction of immunogenic cell death was observed for both linear and macrocyclic GBCAs but not in GdCl3-treated SH-SY5Y cells, with a concentration-dependent increase in extracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) level, high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) protein, and relocation of calreticulin. Furthermore, uptake inhibition studies suggest clathrin-dependent endocytosis by blocking GTPase activity of dynamin proteins in linear gadopentetic acid and accumulation along the cell membrane as seen in TEM images.

papers.title: Coupling Autophagic Flux Blockade With Cuproptosis in a Self-Assembled Nanodrug for Osteosarcoma Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Ding T; Jia M; Yi X; Li X; Xiong Y; Wang M; Dong J; Huang F; He X; Qiao L
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has emerged as a promising approach for osteosarcoma, but its clinical translation is hampered by the complexity of current therapeutic systems. Here, we developed a simple nanodrug composed of Cu2+ and liensinine (Lis) that amplifies tumor cell damage by simultaneously blocking autophagic flux and inducing cuproptosis. Mechanistically, Cu2+ depletes glutathione and disrupts intracellular redox homeostasis, thereby weakening antioxidant defenses and increasing copper-associated mitochondrial stress. This process is accompanied by FDX1 upregulation and cuproptosis-associated mitochondrial dysfunction. In parallel, liensinine impairs lysosomal integrity and blocks autophagosome clearance, thereby preventing the efficient removal of damaged mitochondria and allowing ROS accumulation to persist. Sustained oxidative stress then activates caspase-3, which cleaves GSDME to generate the pore-forming GSDME-N fragment, resulting in plasma membrane permeabilization and subsequent release of damage-associated molecular patterns, thereby enhancing hallmarks of immunogenic cell death and facilitating dendritic cell maturation. In vivo, Cu-Lis suppresses osteosarcoma growth, increases intratumoral immune-cell infiltration, and reduces pulmonary metastasis. Collectively, this work provides a streamlined strategy that integrates autophagic flux blockade with cuproptosis to potentiate antitumor immunity against osteosarcoma.

papers.title: Prohibitin 1 orchestrates mitochondrial-ER crosstalk via the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R axis to drive malignancy in gastric cancer.
papers.authors: Miao Y; Wang X; Huang Y; Zhang Y; Liu Z; Yin H; Liu C; Wang Y; Yin H; Lai Y; Zhang F; Yang S; Li W
papers.abstract: Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membranes (MAMs), serving as critical hubs for mitochondrial-ER interactions, play a pivotal role in cancer progression. Prohibitin 1 (PHB1), an inner mitochondrial membrane protein, contributes to tumorigenesis by regulating energy metabolism and structural integrity. This study aimed to explore the association between PHB1 and MAMs structural integrity, as well as the downstream signaling potentially involved in gastric cancer (GC) metastasis. We analyzed the expression profiles of PHB1/PHB2 in GC tissue using the TCGA database. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect PHB1/PHB2 protein expression in GC tissues, normal gastric tissues, and greater omental metastasis tissues, and to assess their correlation with clinicopathological features. Immunofluorescence and proximity ligation assay (PLA) were used to observe the co-localization of PHB1 with the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 complex. Live-cell Ca2+ imaging, ATP/ROS detection, and mitochondrial functional assays (mPTP opening/MMP) were employed to evaluate calcium flux and energy metabolism changes. Transmission electron microscopy and Western blot were utilized to analyze MAMs structural integrity. The specific VDAC1 inhibitor VBIT-12 and the calcium chelator BAPTA-AM were used to validate the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R signaling axis and the causal relationship between PHB1-dependent MAMs signalling and the downstream cellular phenotypes. A nude mouse xenograft model was established to validate in vivo functions. TCGA analysis confirmed that both PHB1 and PHB2 were overexpressed in GC tissue. PHB1 expression significantly correlated with tumor stage, while PHB2 expression correlated with demographic characteristics. Moreover, the expression of PHB1 was significantly higher than that of PHB2 in omental metastasis tissues. PHB1 overexpression enhanced its co-localization and interaction with the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 complex, thereby regulating Ca2+ flux from the ER to mitochondria. In addition, PHB1 overexpression increased ATP production, and drove cytoskeletal remodeling, thereby promoting malignant progression. Conversely, PHB1 knockdown disrupted the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 axis, leading to MAMs structural dissociation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Furthermore, BAPTA-AM blocked the OE-PHB1-induced enhancement of CDC42 expression, cytoskeletal remodeling. Notably, treatment with VBIT-12 in PHB1-overexpressing cells significantly reversed the pro-tumorigenic effects of PHB1, reduced PHB1 protein levels, and diminished its association with the GRP75-IP3R complex, suggesting that VDAC1 integrity is critical for PHB1-mediated effects. In summary, PHB1 is associated with MAMs structural integrity and functionally coupled to the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R complex in a VDAC1-integrity-associated manner. This subsequently modulates calcium homeostasis, mitochondrial energy metabolism, and cytoskeletal remodeling, ultimately driving GC progression. These findings suggest a novel mechanism by which PHB1 may promote GC progression through its association with MAMs function involving the VDAC1 complex, providing a theoretical basis for further investigation of therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: MicroRNA core machinery maintains mitochondrial integrity to empower cancer escape from natural killer cell cytotoxicity.
papers.authors: Chen JY; Zhao ZF; Zhao HX; Zou M; Qi CJ; Peng ZG; Song TY; Cang Y
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells offer a promising off-the-shelf platform for cancer immunotherapy, yet their clinical efficacy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic resistance. Here, we show that loss of core microRNA (miRNA) machinery components, Argonaute‑2 (AGO2) or Ankyrin Repeat Domain 52 (ANKRD52), renders tumor cells hypersensitive to NK cell-mediated killing in both co-culture and xenograft models. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of Ago2 or Ankrd52 impairs miRNA-mediated silencing of critical mitochondrial apoptotic regulators and NK-cell-associated ligands in tumor cells, exemplified by the disrupted repression of pro-apoptotic Bim transcripts by miR-24 and miR-29b, thereby unleashing rapid TNF-α-driven apoptosis. Additionally, metabolic and ultrastructural analyses demonstrate collapsed membrane potential, diminished ATP levels, and fragmented mitochondria in Ago2- or Ankrd52-mutant tumor cells, accompanied by a lower apoptotic threshold upon TNF-α or NK cell challenge. Genome‑wide CRISPR library screen further revealed a selective fitness dependency on mitochondrial electron‑transport and ATP‑synthase genes in mutant tumor cells. Collectively, these findings define defective miRNA machinery as a tumor‑intrinsic vulnerability that couples mitochondrial fragility with increased NK-mediated cytotoxicity, nominate miRNA‑pathway status as a predictive biomarker, and propose that co‑targeting mitochondrial metabolism or apoptosis may potentiate NK‑cell therapies.
